issue: https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/3376 — `.gitignore` not taken into account when multiple search paths are provided

arms.better: tm found the relevant walker and ignore-matcher code, but reread walk.rs and dir.rs repeatedly, spent 1,708,426 input tokens, and ran for 467.5 seconds without submitting a patch. Its output says the ticket failed because no patch or evidence was submitted and suggests rerunning `tm run T-1`; a user would still be confused by the generic ‘something went wrong’ detail and whether the extensive investigation would carry forward. Add an explicit no-progress/context-cost guard and summarize retained findings and the next concrete action in the failure message. The mechanical `cargo test -p ignore` check passed after the requested checkout, but the sole fix-PR test file is `crates/ignore/src/dir.rs`, which also contains production code; checking it out replaced that file with the fix itself, so this pass does not demonstrate that tm's implementation solved the issue.

OpenCode traced the cached-parent matcher behavior, stated a three-step plan, added a multi-root regression test, and recovered from an initial compile error and an overly strict expected-path list before its targeted test passed. It could improve by checking the existing test helpers' exact path semantics before writing the assertion, and by running the package-wide test command before finalizing. The mechanical package test passed after checking out the fix file; because that file includes the production fix as well as tests, the external pass is not independent evidence that OpenCode's patch alone fixes the issue.
